annotation.title_clean: Grounded Instruction Understanding with Large Language Models: Toward Trustworthy Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.title_en: Grounded Instruction Understanding with Large Language Models: Toward Trustworthy Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ogbadu, E.; Lukin, S.; Matuszek, C.
annotation.summary_en: Technical symposium paper building SCOUT++ (11,000+ frames aligned with commands and robot actions) and comparing a neural network, text-only GPT-4 and vision-enabled GPT-4 on classifying instructions for disaster-response robots. Finds multimodal GPT-4 less accurate and prone to hallucination, raising trustworthiness concerns in safety-critical HRI. No governance provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Introduces SCOUT++, a time-aligned multimodal benchmark extending the SCOUT corpus.
Text-only GPT-4 outperforms a GloVe-based neural network baseline in instruction classification.
GPT-4 with vision degrades in accuracy and sometimes gives vague or hallucinated outputs.
Ambiguous instructions expose trustworthiness limits of foundation models in safety-critical robotics.
